sources.title: Improving Lives and Livelihoods: Poverty and Equity Assessment for El Salvador 2024
sources.temporal_coverage: Poverty and climate analysis published in 2024; includes historical exposure and forward-looking risks.
sources.methodology: Country poverty assessment combining household and climate evidence.
sources.limitations: Conflict links are conditional risks, not measured outcomes.

sources.title: Contribuciones Nacionalmente Determinadas de El Salvador 2025
sources.organization: Government of El Salvador, Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources
sources.temporal_coverage: 2025 NDC; adaptation objectives and strategic targets mainly cover 2030–2035.
sources.methodology: Government NDC based on sector and territorial vulnerability analysis and interagency consultation.
sources.limitations: Commitments and planned systems are not evidence of completed results.

sources.title: The World Food Programme's Contribution to Improving the Prospects for Peace in El Salvador
sources.organization: Stockholm International Peace Research Institute, with World Food Programme field research
sources.temporal_coverage: Field research conducted in March 2019; findings describe the then-current program and conflict context.
sources.methodology: Two-week country case study using interviews, focus groups, programme review and project-site visits.

sources.title: Evaluación de Vulnerabilidad y Adaptación al Cambio Climático en El Salvador
sources.organization: Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources of El Salvador; ESSA Technologies Ltd. and associates
sources.temporal_coverage: Municipal vulnerability baseline and projections for 2021–2050 and 2071–2100, published February 2018.
sources.methodology: Indicator-based two-territory municipal assessment with participatory adaptation prioritization.
sources.limitations: Focuses on the AMSS and selected Eastern Dry Corridor municipalities, not all of El Salvador.

claims.locator: PDF p. 65, paragraph beginning 'Similarly, intense floods'.
claims.paraphrase: The assessment says floods and extended droughts affecting food security could exacerbate conflict and migration.
claims.limitations: Conditional risk statement, not a measured outcome.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: It explicitly says these shocks could exacerbate conflict and migration.

claims.locator: PDF p. 65, paragraph beginning 'Extended periods of drought'.
claims.paraphrase: Dry Corridor drought followed by intense rain disrupts planting and harvests; the assessment reports agricultural labor-income losses for 13% of rural households and particular exposure among subsistence farmers.
claims.limitations: The percentage is a dated cited estimate.

claims.paraphrase: The assessment places 73% of districts in high-drought zones, concentrated in high-poverty Usulután, Ahuachapán, Cabañas and La Unión departments.
claims.limitations: Uses a 2012 FAO map and legacy boundaries.

claims.paraphrase: The 2025 NDC says 88.7% of national territory faces disaster risk; Cabañas, Morazán and Ahuachapán have high vulnerability combining socioeconomic factors, weak basic-service access and environmental stress.
institutions: Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources
claims.limitations: National NDC assessment; the passage does not disaggregate by municipality.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 49–50, section 4.5.3 on human mobility.
claims.paraphrase: The NDC sets a 2030–2035 objective to strengthen adaptation, food security and community resilience to reduce environmental and climate-related migration, and proposes a data system on such movements.
affected_groups: people considering environmental or climate-related migration
institutions: Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources
claims.limitations: This is a planned policy objective and information system, not an evaluated result.

claims.locator: PDF p. 25, National Coordination Mechanism on Human Mobility.
claims.paraphrase: The NDC describes an interagency mobility mechanism coordinated by Foreign Affairs and MARN, with agriculture, migration, housing and territorial-government bodies, intended to connect mobility, environment and climate agendas.
claims.limitations: The NDC states the mechanism's purpose, not its effectiveness.

claims.paraphrase: The 2019 case study describes Dry Corridor rural communities as vulnerable to climate impacts and gang-related conflict; during a severe drought, small-scale farmers lost most maize harvests while community cohesion was low.
claims.limitations: This is qualitative 2019 program-context research, not a current national estimate.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The case study explicitly describes climate change as a risk multiplier in social-tension and gang-conflict settings during drought.

claims.locator: Executive Summary, PDF p. x; field sites listed on PDF p. 14.
claims.paraphrase: The study reports that gang dynamics required WFP to negotiate program access and beneficiaries to obtain permission to participate; field visits included San Miguel, Uluazapa, Jiquilisco, Ozatlán, Usulután, Suchitoto, Agua Caliente and San Salvador.
claims.limitations: Access constraints and site list reflect fieldwork in March 2019.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Gang dynamics constrained program access and affected beneficiaries' ability to participate.

claims.paraphrase: The case study reports that WFP resilience activities brought landless agricultural day laborers and smallholders into communication with landowners and local government, with observed contributions to social cohesion and women's empowerment.
claims.limitations: Qualitative assessment of specific WFP interventions; not a population-wide impact estimate.

claims.locator: PDF p. 63, discussion of the historical flood and landslide record.
claims.paraphrase: The assessment ranks San Salvador, Soyapango, Ilopango and Cuscatancingo as most vulnerable to heavy-rain flooding and landslides; San Salvador recorded 209 floods and 79 landslides during 1960–2015.
claims.limitations: Historical counts are not current risk rates.

claims.locator: PDF p. 90, Eastern Dry Corridor agricultural vulnerability analysis.
claims.paraphrase: During three years of rainfall anomalies, maize and sorghum yields fell 43% and bean yields 29% in La Unión and Morazán; over 90% of producers used maize-bean-sorghum systems.
claims.limitations: The report cites 2013–2016 yield figures; not current estimates.

claims.locator: PDF p. 85, results for selected Eastern Dry Corridor municipalities.
claims.paraphrase: Municipalities with more land in staple grains tend to have higher climate vulnerability, while adaptive capacity is very low across the studied Eastern Dry Corridor municipalities.
claims.limitations: Limited to municipalities selected for this 2018 assessment.

access_audit.locator: Opened the original 97-page assessment; claims use PDF pp. 65, 69, and 74–75.
access_audit.notes: Cover identifies the 2024 assessment; conditional links are not recast as observed causal outcomes.
access_audit.reuse_terms: World Bank permits attributed noncommercial reproduction; concise paraphrases only.

access_audit.locator: Opened the original 82-page 2025 NDC; claims use PDF pp. 16–17, 25, and 49–50.
access_audit.notes: Commitments and strategic objectives are recorded as plans, not delivered capacity.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrases only.

access_audit.locator: Opened the original 48-page SIPRI working paper; cited findings are in the executive summary and fieldwork methods on PDF pp. ix–x and 14.
access_audit.notes: Qualitative fieldwork took place in March 2019; statements describe that period.
access_audit.reuse_terms: SIPRI publication states all rights reserved; derived short paraphrases only.

access_audit.locator: Opened the original 173-page MARN assessment; claims use PDF pp. 63, 85 and 90.
access_audit.notes: The report is dated February 2018 and evaluates the AMSS and selected Eastern Dry Corridor municipalities.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrases only.

access_audit.notes: Search-result text was not used as evidence; the separately opened World Bank assessment and SIPRI full text supply the retained findings.

search_audit.query: El Salvador Dry Corridor municipality drought poverty climate risk subnational report 2024 2025 MARN WB
search_audit.outcome: Opened the World Bank assessment, 2025 government NDC and 2018 MARN territorial assessment; retained dated municipality and department evidence.

search_audit.query: El Salvador climate drought food insecurity gang violence conflict migration primary study report
search_audit.outcome: The 2024 poverty assessment states a conditional flood/drought–food-security link to conflict and migration; 2019 SIPRI/WFP field research describes the Dry Corridor risk-multiplier context.

search_audit.query: El Salvador gang insecurity humanitarian access constraints climate adaptation rural Dry Corridor communities
search_audit.outcome: 2019 SIPRI/WFP fieldwork reports gang-related access negotiation and beneficiary-permission constraints; it does not establish a current national climate-program access pattern.

search_audit.query: El Salvador climate adaptation resilience capacity Dry Corridor migration local farmers community NDC
search_audit.outcome: The NDC sets future mobility and territorial adaptation priorities; MARN assessed municipal capacity and SIPRI/WFP reports historical cohesion contributions.

gaps: The sources do not establish a climate cause of gang violence; the 2024 World Bank statement is explicitly conditional, while the SIPRI/WFP nexus description is a qualitative 2019 context analysis.
No current subnational assessment was found showing how insecurity constrains climate-adaptation implementation in 2026; SIPRI/WFP program-access observations date to 2019.
The 2023 Climate-Fragility Risk Brief PDF exceeded direct retrieval limits and was not used; the WFP Central American Dry Corridor report PDF returned 403 and only its landing page was opened.
